stem:
Pihu plans to spot Orion from an open terrace at 9:00 p.m. Orion is above the horizon for her place and date, but thick cloud covers the whole sky and bright courtyard lamps stay on.

Which judgment about seeing Orion that evening is correct?

options.text: Orion will not be clearly visible because clouds and bright lamps block a clear dark sky.
Orion is visible tonight even though thick cloud covers the whole sky.
More of Orion's stars will appear after the courtyard lamps are switched on brighter.
Orion can be seen tonight through the cloud cover because the sky looks black.

teacher.key_rationale: Night-sky viewing needs a clear dark sky and an open view. Clouds and bright lamps prevent seeing Orion clearly. A blocked view, brighter lights, or a black-looking cloudy sky do not make the constellation visible.
